description: Start one structured program/argv command under Runtime supervision and return a command handle after policy, approval, and sandbox initialization succeed. Use this for commands that may outlast one tool call.

propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name, path relative to cwd, or absolute local executable. Same resolution and isolation as run_command.
propertyDescriptions.args: Literal structured argv, including multiline code. For cmd /c the complete command must be one argument; no automatic shell-string joining.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Existing absolute or workspace-relative directory whose normalized real path stays inside the workspace.
propertyDescriptions.intent: Declared command purpose, not permission. Use test, build or verify for validation.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Optional validation category. Missing verify/test categories default to custom; build defaults to build. Inapplicable or invalid metadata is normalized without blocking execution.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested total command-phase timeout. It remains attached to the process across later polls; Runtime returns the effective capped budget.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Use for a long-running build, test, verification, install or program, with the same flat contract and network rules as run_command. Prefer direct test output over a filtering pipeline; Runtime returns execution status separately from validation passed/failed/unknown. After status running, use poll_command for bounded waits and cancel_command when no longer needed. Do not complete the task before observing its terminal result. Missing validation metadata is normalized once, and remains attached across polls.
